title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial measuring whether constrained prompting combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback (generate→verify→repair, one allowed repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents (four intent families), shared_initial_candidate semantics, model declared = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Each intent produced one initial generation that was shared across baseline and guarded conditions; the guarded pipeline could invoke at most one additional repair call. Results: baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Only one guarded repair was applied. Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over an already near-ceiling baseline. We highlight the methodological lesson that short baseline-calibration pilots are necessary to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate preregistered power plans. All execution artifacts, runtime metadata, and analysis files are archived in the execution bundle referenced by the preregistration and execution manifests.

sections.introduction:
Natural-language intent interfaces promise to reduce operator burden by letting humans describe desired network changes in free text and then automatically translating those intents into executable device-level configurations. Prior work documents that single-pass LLM outputs can contain syntactic errors, omissions, or semantic violations that risk unsafe or unavailable network states when applied without verification [1],[2],[3]. A dominant defensive architecture is a generate→verify→repair pipeline: an LLM produces a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks intent-level invariants derived from a formal specification, and an automated repair (or human gate) corrects violations prior to execution [4],[5]. Concurrent security analyses show that unguarded tool-augmented LLM agents can convert false textual claims into harmful actions, motivating deterministic gating [6].

Research question. After an autonomous literature review and preregistration we posed a narrowly scoped confirmatory question: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline in a paired design? The experiment (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) was preregistered and frozen prior to observing any model outputs.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifactized paired confirmatory trial measuring deterministic-verifier pass/fail as the primary endpoint on a programmatically generated synthetic corpus (N=150 paired intents). (2) A complete execution and analysis package showing that, under shared_initial_candidate semantics and a one-repair budget, the guarded pipeline raised the verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (absolute +0.67 pp), a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). (3) A practical methodological recommendation: preregistered NetOps trials should run short baseline-calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects; researchers must explicitly state generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent sampling) because they change the estimand and interpretation.
sections.related_work:
Related literature spans three strands. First, intent-to-configuration research documents persistent difficulty producing verifier-sound artifacts from free text and reports modest semantic-correctness on public benchmarks, motivating post-generation checks and formalization efforts [1],[2]. Second, generate→verify→repair architectures—ranging from verifier-in-the-loop fine-tuning to policy-guided verifier feedback—have demonstrated correctness improvements for infrastructure-as-code and configuration-repair tasks, but reported gains depend strongly on baseline model competence, repair budget, and sampling semantics [4],[7]. Third, security and systems analyses demonstrate claim-to-action vulnerabilities where unchecked LLM outputs combined with tool invocation can lead to harmful actions; these works argue for auditable gating and verifier-aware planning to reduce risk [6],[8].

How this study situates. Our trial operationalizes a narrowly specified guarded architecture and emphasizes preregistration, paired inference, and deterministic-verifier endpoints. Compared to prior work reporting larger guarded-vs-baseline gains, key contrasts here are: (a) shared_initial_candidate execution semantics (one sampled initial candidate reused across conditions), (b) a strict one-repair budget per intent, (c) a single tested model (declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"), and (d) a synthetic verifier-capable task bank limited to small topologies. Those design choices bound the maximal observable marginal benefit of the guarded repair under our estimand and explain compatibility with prior reported gains under different semantics or larger repair budgets.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 and the analysis plan frozen before any model outputs were observed; the preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest. The confirmatory design is paired_binary with primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and an exact two-sided McNemar test as confirmatory inference. Key preregistered constraints included N=150 confirmatory intents, exactly one initial model call per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics), and at most one guarded repair call per intent. Inclusion/exclusion rules (rule-based ambiguity detector, verifier-coverage checks), a deterministic retry policy for provider/API timeouts, and a power plan targeting a +15 percentage-point absolute improvement with ≈80% power were also preregistered.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and inferential meaning. Per the execution contract, for each intent exactly one initial model generation was produced and that identical sampled candidate was used to evaluate both baseline and guarded conditions. The guarded pipeline could invoke at most one additional repair call only if the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate. Inferential implication: the baseline success rate measures the validity of that single sampled candidate, and the guarded vs baseline contrast isolates the marginal effect of applying at most one repair to that identical candidate. This differs from independent-sampling designs where per-condition randomness creates different estimands (average performance under independent draws) and can increase observable differences when sampling variance is larger.

Task generation and corpus. Confirmatory tasks were produced deterministically by the preregistered generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) and cover four intent families: reachability/isolation, ACL-like access changes, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, and uplink switchover patterns. Topologies were restricted to verifier-capable small networks (4–32 nodes). Pre-execution mapping and verifier-coverage unit-tests were applied; no confirmatory exclusions occurred (exclusions = 0). Representative tasks archived in the bundle show difficulty labels ranging from medium to very_hard, required_command_count values up to 6, and required sequencing constraints (e.g., make-before-break, paired-mtu-change).

Model, adapter, and deterministic validator. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses). The execution adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) enforced the one-initial/≤one-repair call budget per intent. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule and returned a boolean pass/fail plus normalized final-configuration text and diagnostics (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes). Important runtime-parameter clarification required by review and explicitly reported here: the archived execution model configuration (model_configuration.json) records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset). Null in the recorded configuration denotes that no numeric temperature or fixed random-seed was enforced by the adapter; therefore model outputs may be nondeterministic across independent API sessions. The model_configuration.json and per-call runtime metadata are archived for inspection.

Execution accounting, retries, and contamination controls. Planned episodes = 300 (150 paired tasks × 2 conditions); completed_episode_count = 300; complete_pair_count = 150. The adapter recorded model_calls_used = 151 (150 shared_initial generations + 1 repair call). Provider-call auditing in the deterministic reconciliation artifact reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 151, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 1, and condition_counts: shared = 150, guarded = 1. Contamination checks reported zero flags; pre-execution mapping unit-tests passed. The missingness policy was not invoked because no provider-call failures or parsing failures occurred.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and provider audit. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. Execution manifest values: model_calls_used = 151 and artifact_hash_count = 1058. Deterministic reconciliation provider_call_audit reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 151; stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 150, repair: 1}; condition_counts = {shared: 150, guarded: 1}. analysis/contamination_summary.csv records no contamination flags and pre-execution unit-tests passed.

Primary numerical outcomes and paired table. The paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline) observed were: n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. The estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). These numeric facts are drawn directly from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv) and the analysis log.

Repair diagnostics and revision iterations. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), consistent with the near-ceiling initial success rate. That single repair converted one initially invalid candidate to a valid configuration under the deterministic validator. Summary revision statistics: median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Validator traces for each episode include validation_before and validation_after states, normalized_configuration strings, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and valid flag; representative traces are provided in execution/scoring/task-00000X-*.json and archived for inspection.

Representative artifact examples. Representative task manifests and shared-initial responses demonstrate typical intents and validator normalization. Example (task-000001): intent — "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600. For safety, shut edge1 down before changing either VLAN or MTU, then restore it to admin up." Shared-initial and both condition responses returned the expected four-command sequence and the validator recorded parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, and valid = true. Similar representative artifacts (tasks 000002–000006) show difficulty labels (medium, hard, hard, very_hard, very_hard, very_hard) and normalized configurations; these artifacts substantiate that the task generator produced nontrivial workflows while the tested model achieved near-ceiling correctness on the frozen corpus.

Sensitivity and missingness checks. The preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats missing guarded outputs as failures was not invoked because failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0 and unscorable episodes = 0. No exclusions or parse failures occurred. Contamination and mapping unit-tests passed before batch execution; analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains an empty flag set.

Concise numerical interpretation. The guarded pipeline's observed marginal gain (≈0.67 pp) is numerically tiny and statistically non-significant under the preregistered test. Given the baseline's near-perfect pass rate, the run experienced a ceiling effect that invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (planned detectable effect = 15 pp). The bootstrap CI upper bound (0.02) quantifies that, on this corpus and under shared_initial_candidate semantics, any true marginal improvement of the guarded pipeline is small (<2 percentage points at the 95% CI level).
sections.discussion:
Ceiling effect and implications for preregistration. The preregistered power calculation assumed a substantially lower baseline; baseline_success_rate = 0.9933 left almost no headroom for the guarded repair to show a large absolute improvement. Practical implication: preregistered NetOps trials should include a short baseline-calibration pilot (e.g., few dozen tasks) to estimate baseline competence for the selected model, prompt style, and generator difficulty and to adjust N or task difficulty accordingly.

Semantics-driven estimand differences. Shared_initial_candidate semantics reduce sampling variance and isolate the marginal benefit of a repair applied to an identical initial candidate, but they do not capture condition-level randomness. Independent-sampling designs or larger repair budgets yield different estimands—expected performance averaged over independent draws or repair-driven robustness gains—which can produce larger observable gains when baseline sampling variance is greater. Practitioners must therefore match experimental semantics to operational questions: marginal-repair value for a fixed generated candidate versus averaged robustness across independent generations.

Operational value beyond binary verification. Deterministic guarded workflows provide operational affordances not captured by a simple pass/fail metric: auditable normalized configurations, concise diagnostic traces useful for operator triage, deterministic verdicts that support gating policies, and standardized repair prompts that simplify human review. Even when marginal verifier-pass improvements are small on constrained corpora, these operational artifacts can reduce manual triage time and support safer execution pipelines.

Threats to validity and external-generalizability limits. Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate semantics and the adapter-enforced call budget were followed and provider-call audits confirm no cross-condition leakage. Construct validity: deterministic validator pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; mapping unit-tests mitigated but do not eliminate the risk of mis-evaluation. External validity: the experiment used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), a synthetic task bank, and small topologies (4–32 nodes); results do not generalize to different models, richer CLIs, or production WANs without further study. Conclusion validity: the preregistered detectable effect assumption (15 pp) was not met due to an unexpectedly high baseline; confidence intervals and p-values are reported without overclaiming.

Recommendations for future designs. Based on archived artifacts we recommend: (1) run a short baseline-calibration pilot and adjust sample size or task difficulty before fixing N, (2) state generation semantics explicitly in preregistration, (3) preregister repair-budget sensitivity analyses (e.g., multiple repairs permitted), (4) archive and publish mapping/verifier unit-tests prior to batch runs, and (5) report provider-call audits (model_calls_used, stage_counts, cache_miss/hit) to document execution budgets and stage-level behavior. Experiment variants that address external validity include independent per-condition sampling, larger repair budgets, multiple model families, and scaling to larger topologies with higher verifier coverage.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting with constrained-template prompting plus a single deterministic-verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministically generated synthetic corpus with declared model gpt-5-mini and validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased the verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically tiny and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline calibration to avoid ceiling effects and preserve statistical power. Technically, our artifacts bound the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics; evaluating alternative semantics, larger repair budgets, model diversity, and production-scale topologies remains important future work.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only the declared model gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
